prompt: Triangle $ABC$ has lengths $AB=20$, $AC=14$, $BC=22$. The median from $B$ intersects $AC$ at $M$ and the angle bisector from $C$ intersects $AB$ at $N$ and the median from $B$ at $P$. Let $\frac pq=\frac{[AMPN]}{[ABC]}$ for positive integers $p,q$ coprime. Note that $[ABC]$ denotes the area of triangle $ABC$. Find $p+q$.

solutions.title: Menelaus and area ratios
solutions.body:
By the angle bisector theorem $AN:NB=CA:CB=14:22=7:11$, so $BN/BA=\frac{11}{18}$. Since $M$ is the midpoint of $AC$, $[ABM]=\frac12[ABC]$.

Menelaus in triangle $ABM$ with the line $N$–$P$–$C$: $\dfrac{AN}{NB}\cdot\dfrac{BP}{PM}\cdot\dfrac{MC}{CA}=1$, i.e. $\dfrac7{11}\cdot\dfrac{BP}{PM}\cdot\dfrac12=1$, so $\dfrac{BP}{PM}=\dfrac{22}{7}$ and $\dfrac{BP}{BM}=\dfrac{22}{29}$.

The quadrilateral $AMPN$ is triangle $ABM$ minus triangle $BNP$, and
$$\frac{[BNP]}{[ABM]}=\frac{BN}{BA}\cdot\frac{BP}{BM}=\frac{11}{18}\cdot\frac{22}{29}=\frac{121}{261}.$$
Hence $\dfrac{[AMPN]}{[ABC]}=\dfrac12\left(1-\dfrac{121}{261}\right)=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{140}{261}=\dfrac{70}{261}$, and $p+q=70+261=331$.

**Answer: 331**

prompt: Consider the pyramid $OABC$. Let the equilateral triangle $ABC$ with side length $6$ be the base. Also $9=OA=OB=OC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$. Find the square of the distance from $M$ to $OC$.

solutions.title: Triangle OMC
solutions.body:
$MC$ is a median of the equilateral triangle: $MC=3\sqrt3$. Since $OA=OB$ and $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$, $OM\perp AB$ and $OM^2=OA^2-AM^2=81-9=72$.

In triangle $OMC$ the sides are $OC=9$, $MC=3\sqrt3$, $OM=6\sqrt2$. By the law of cosines at $C$:
$$72=81+27-2\cdot9\cdot3\sqrt3\cos C\ \Rightarrow\ \cos C=\frac{36}{54\sqrt3}=\frac{2}{3\sqrt3},\quad \cos^2C=\frac4{27}.$$
The distance from $M$ to line $OC$ is $MC\sin C$, so its square is $27\left(1-\frac4{27}\right)=23$.

**Answer: 23**

solutions.title: Using the height of the pyramid
solutions.body:
Let $D$ be the centre of $ABC$; then $CD=2\sqrt3$ and $OD\perp$ base with $OD^2=81-12=69$. In the vertical plane through $O$, $D$, $M$, $C$ (these lie in one plane because $M$, $D$, $C$ are collinear), triangle $OMC$ has base $MC=3\sqrt3$ and height $OD=\sqrt{69}$, so its area is $\frac12\cdot3\sqrt3\cdot\sqrt{69}$. The same area equals $\frac12\cdot OC\cdot h$ with $h$ the required distance: $9h=3\sqrt3\sqrt{69}=9\sqrt{23}$, so $h^2=23$.

**Answer: 23**

prompt: In triangle $ABC$, $E\in AC$, $D\in AB$ and $P=BE\cap CD$. Given that $[BPC]=12$, while the areas of triangle $BPD$, triangle $CPE$ and quadrilateral $AEPD$ are all the same, equal to $x$. Find the value of $x$.

solutions.title: Area ratios along AP
solutions.body:
Join $AP$ and let $y=[ADP]$, $z=[AEP]$, so $x=y+z$ (the quadrilateral $AEPD$).

Triangles $ADP$ and $BDP$ share the vertex $P$ and have bases on $AB$, and so do $ADC$ and $BDC$:
$$\frac yx=\frac{AD}{DB}=\frac{[ADC]}{[BDC]}=\frac{y+z+x}{x+12}=\frac{2x}{x+12}.$$
Similarly
$$\frac zx=\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{[ABE]}{[CBE]}=\frac{y+x+z}{12+x}=\frac{2x}{x+12}.$$
Adding, $\dfrac{y+z}{x}=1=\dfrac{4x}{x+12}$, so $x=4$.

**Answer: 4**

prompt: Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$ with circumradius $15$. Let $G$ be the centroid of $ABC$ and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. If $BC=18$ and $\angle MOA=150^\circ$, find the area of $OMG$.

solutions.title: Area of AOM, then ratio along the median
solutions.body:
$OM\perp BC$ and $BM=9$, $OB=15$, so $OM=\sqrt{15^2-9^2}=12$. With $OA=15$ and $\angle MOA=150^\circ$:
$$[AOM]=\tfrac12\cdot12\cdot15\cdot\sin150^\circ=45.$$
The centroid $G$ lies on the median $AM$ with $GM=\frac13AM$. Triangles $OMG$ and $OMA$ share the vertex $O$ and have bases on line $AM$, so $[OMG]=\frac13[OMA]=15$.

**Answer: 15**

prompt: Consider the cyclic quadrilateral with sides $1,4,8,7$ in that order. What is its circumdiameter? Let the answer be of the form $a\sqrt b+c$, for $b$ square free. Find $a+b+c$.

solutions.title: Reflect a vertex
solutions.body:
Let the quadrilateral be $ABCD$ with $AB=1$, $BC=4$, $CD=8$, $DA=7$. Reflect $D$ in the perpendicular bisector of $AC$ to get $D'$. This reflection preserves the circle and the side of line $AC$ containing $D$, so $ABCD'$ is also a cyclic quadrilateral (in this order), with $AD'=CD=8$ and $CD'=AD=7$.

Apply the law of cosines to the diagonal $BD'$ in triangles $ABD'$ and $CBD'$, with $\alpha=\angle BAD'$ and $\angle BCD'=180^\circ-\alpha$:
$$1+64-16\cos\alpha=BD'^2=16+49+56\cos\alpha\ \Rightarrow\ \cos\alpha=0.$$
So $\alpha=90^\circ$, and $BD'$ is a diameter with $BD'^2=1+64=65$.

The circumdiameter is $\sqrt{65}=1\cdot\sqrt{65}+0$, so $a+b+c=1+65+0=66$.

**Answer: 66**

prompt: There is a point $D$ on side $AC$ of acute triangle $\triangle ABC$. Let $AM$ be the median drawn from $A$ (so $M$ is on $BC$) and $CH$ be the altitude drawn from $C$ (so $H$ is on $AB$). Let $I$ be the intersection of $AM$ and $CH$, and let $K$ be the intersection of $AM$ and line segment $BD$. We know that $AK=8$, $BK=8$, and $MK=6$. Find the length of $AI$.

solutions.title: A parallelogram
solutions.body:
Draw the line through $C$ parallel to $AM$ and let it meet line $BD$ at $E$. Since $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$ and $KM\parallel EC$, $K$ is the midpoint of $BE$ and $EC=2KM=12$.

Triangle $ABK$ is isosceles ($AK=BK=8$), so the midpoint $H'$ of $AB$ satisfies $KH'\perp AB$. In triangle $ABE$, $KH'$ joins the midpoints of $BE$ and $BA$, so $KH'\parallel AE$. Hence $AE\perp AB$, and also $CH\perp AB$, so $AE\parallel CH$, i.e. $AE\parallel IC$.

Together with $AI\parallel EC$, the quadrilateral $AICE$ is a parallelogram, so $AI=EC=12$.

**Answer: 12**

prompt: Consider quadrilateral $ABCD$. Given that $\angle DAC=70^\circ$, $\angle BAC=40^\circ$, $\angle BDC=20^\circ$, $\angle CBD=35^\circ$. Let $P$ be the intersection of $AC$ and $BD$. Find $\angle BPC$.

solutions.title: A is the circumcentre of BCD
solutions.body:
In triangle $BCD$, $\angle CBD=35^\circ$ and $\angle BDC=20^\circ$. If $O$ is its circumcentre, the inscribed angle theorem gives $\angle COD=2\cdot35^\circ=70^\circ=\angle CAD$ and $\angle COB=2\cdot20^\circ=40^\circ=\angle CAB$. The point seeing $CD$ under $70^\circ$ and $CB$ under $40^\circ$ (with $AC$ between $AD$ and $AB$) is unique, so $A=O$ is the centre of the circle through $B,C,D$ and $AB=AC=AD$.

Triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with apex angle $40^\circ$, so $\angle ACB=\frac{180^\circ-40^\circ}2=70^\circ$. In triangle $PBC$: $\angle PCB=\angle ACB=70^\circ$, $\angle PBC=\angle DBC=35^\circ$, hence
$$\angle BPC=180^\circ-70^\circ-35^\circ=75^\circ.$$

**Answer: 75**

solutions.title: Inscribed angle on the circle
solutions.body:
With $A$ the centre and $E$ the point of the circle diametrically opposite to $C$ (on ray $CA$ beyond $A$), the angle between chords $BD$ and $CE$ meeting at $P$ is half the sum of the arcs they cut off: $\angle BPC=\frac12(\overset{\frown}{BC}+\overset{\frown}{DE})=\frac12(40^\circ+(180^\circ-70^\circ))=75^\circ$.

**Answer: 75**

prompt: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral with circumcenter $O$ and circumradius $7$. $AB$ intersects $CD$ at $E$, $DA$ intersects $CB$ at $F$. $OE=13$, $OF=14$. Let $\cos\angle FOE=\frac pq$, with $p,q$ coprime. Find $p+q$.

solutions.title: Power of a point and the Miquel point
solutions.body:
The powers of $E$ and $F$ with respect to the circle are
$$\mathrm{pow}(E)=13^2-7^2=120,\qquad \mathrm{pow}(F)=14^2-7^2=147 .$$
Let $X$ be the point on $EF$ with $\angle CXE=\angle CDF$. Since $ABCD$ is cyclic, $\angle CBA=180^\circ-\angle ADC=\angle CDF$, so $\angle EBC+\angle CXE=(180^\circ-\angle CBA)+\angle CDF=180^\circ$: $BEXC$ is cyclic, and likewise $CXFD$ is cyclic. The circle $BEXC$ and the circumcircle share the chord $BC$, so the power of $F$ with respect to circle $BEXC$ equals $FC\cdot FB=147$; similarly the power of $E$ with respect to circle $CXFD$ is $120$. Therefore
$$EX\cdot EF=120,\qquad FX\cdot FE=147,$$
and adding, $EF^2=120+147=267$.

Law of cosines in triangle $EOF$:
$$267=13^2+14^2-2\cdot13\cdot14\cos\angle EOF\ \Rightarrow\ \cos\angle EOF=\frac{365-267}{364}=\frac{98}{364}=\frac7{26}.$$
So $p+q=7+26=33$.

**Answer: 33**
